name_or_item: Deepdale Viaduct, Yorkshire (iron trestle, 158 ft high)

source_ref: Cudworth, ICE Minutes of Proceedings 85 (1886) 340-342

name_or_item: Hownes Gill Viaduct, County Durham (firebrick arch)

name_or_item: Plain line, North Eastern Railway (benchmark)

name_or_item: Forth Bridge, Scotland (steel cantilever, 1890)

name_or_item: Forth Bridge, Scotland (steel cantilever, 1890)

source_ref: Herald (Glasgow), 19 February 1993, quoting ScotRail maintenance figures

name_or_item: Highways Agency trunk-road structures (England)

source_ref: Arup for the Office of Rail Regulation, 'Review asset policy, stewardship and management of structures', March 2011, §4.3.3

name_or_item: Transport for London structures

name_or_item: Masonry and iron road bridges: share of capital, London County Council

source_ref: Derived from the 1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica LCC table (maintenance / net capital expenditure)

scope: lowest of nine LCC Thames bridges, 1907-08

name_or_item: Wrought-iron and steel bridges: painting as share of first cost

name_or_item: Wrought-iron and steel bridges: painting as share of first cost
scope: upper bound; painting at 1s per square yard on a five-year cycle
source_ref: Thorpe, 'The Anatomy of Bridgework' (1906), ch. XV, p. 168
notes: Steel with shorter painting intervals 'somewhat higher'. Cast iron less; cast iron encased in masonry 'practically nothing'.

name_or_item: Bridges: target annual maintenance as share of gross replacement cost

name_or_item: Network Rail tunnels, Great Britain (all lining materials)
